summary: Dalian PP futures +USD 75 vs Sep 30 settle; Exxon PP block copo settles 1,450-1,500 CIF to Vietnam
Domestic unmoved: NSRP 114G eased slightly; market flat as sellers await China's new quotes
Sabic copo 36/37/310MK10 still VND 37,900-38,500 domestically vs 1,435-1,450 CIF import offers
paras: According to Platts assessments released today, October 8, in Northeast Asia the general price level for all PP grades held flat this week because China is on holiday. Similarly, in Southeast Asia, PP prices of all grades held flat from last week, with PP yarn/injection at USD 1,310/tonne/CFR, BOPP at USD 1,330/tonne/CFR, IPP film at USD 1,410/tonne/CFR and PP block copolymer at USD 1,360/tonne/CFR.

PP prices in Asia remained stable amid cautious market sentiment, with both sellers and buyers in the region awaiting new quotations from Chinese sellers after the holiday. Two Thai companies, SCG Chemicals Public Co. Ltd. and PTT Global Chemical Public Co. Ltd., have entered a detailed due-diligence phase to confirm plans to form a joint venture covering their olefins and polyolefins (PP, PE resin) businesses. In Vietnam, domestic supply and operating rates at local producers remained stable.

Today, according to sources, settled transaction prices for Exxon Mobil PP block copolymer shipped from Singapore to Vietnam can be done at USD 1,450-1,500/tonne/CIF depending on grade and volume, although yesterday some distributors offered at USD 1,500-1,530/tonne/CIF. SCG of Thailand's distributor offered PP copolymer to the Vietnamese market in VND, equivalent to about USD 1,510/tonne/CIF at USD conversion. In the domestic market, traders are offering these grades at VND 43,500-44,000/kg including VAT.

China's market resumed operations today. On the Dalian Commodity Exchange, China's PP futures jumped USD 75/tonne from the September 30 settlement price — before the holiday. Even so, no new PP offers to Vietnam have been recorded.

Notably, in Vietnam the domestic PP market today remained fairly stable and has not yet moved with the new developments in the Chinese market. NSRP's leading distributor Marubeni even offered PP 114G to some large northern customers today at VND 38,800/kg including VAT, down a further VND 200/kg from the start of the week (VND 400/kg lower than late last week), remaining the most competitively priced domestic PP yarn.

According to some sources, Vietnamese-plant PP homopolymer (yarn/injection) is being offered for export by distributors to the Indonesian market at high prices of USD 1,390-1,400/tonne/CIF. With high export prices achievable, some plants — typically Hyosung Vina — are currently prioritizing exports, leaving limited domestic offer volumes. Offers for PP yarn from domestic plants such as BSR and Hyosung Vina remained flat in the VND 39,500-40,000/kg including VAT range…

On imported PP, northern sellers were still recorded offering Sabic PP copolymer 36MK10, 37MK10 and 310MK10 at only VND 37,900-38,500/kg including VAT; South Korea's SK PP homopolymer at only VND 37,500/kg including VAT and SK PP random at VND 38,500/kg including VAT… Other traders raised each of these grades this week by about VND 500-700/kg, to VND 38,400-39,000/kg including VAT, after fairly large volumes were consumed last week.

“Import offers for Sabic PP copolymer grades 36MK10 and 37MK10… to Vietnam are now high, up to USD 1,435-1,450/tonne/CIF, so the fact that many sellers offer domestically at cheap levels of VND 38,000-38,500/kg including VAT — lower even than PP yarn — may be because of stock imported when prices were cheap. By reports, the domestic PP copolymer market has recently consumed fairly slowly. Meanwhile, some trading companies holding off-grade (OG) PP copolymer of SK and Hanwha (South Korea) origin, in bulk, are offering at cheap prices of only VND 32,000-33,000/kg including VAT, putting competitive pressure on prime PP copolymer,” a northern source analyzed.

summary: Qamar LLDPE & HDPE Film both USD 1,480 ex-bonded HCMC; Sabic FJ00952 re-export 1,340 CIF Hai Phong
High Sabic import offers met buyer resistance; LDPE uptrend stalling as buyers turn cautious
Domestic PE flat from yesterday; transactions flat-to-lower w/w; Petrochina LLDPE 2020F VND 39,400
paras: According to Platts assessments released today, October 8, in Northeast Asia the general price level for all PE grades held flat from last week, mainly because China was on holiday for the first three days of the week. In Southeast Asia, PE prices of all grades also held stable from last week, with HDPE Film/yarn/blow/injection at USD 1,270-1,280/tonne/CFR, LLDPE Film at USD 1,220/tonne/CFR, metallocene LLDPE C6 steady at USD 1,370/tonne/CFR, and LDPE at USD 1,590/tonne/CFR. The cause was limited trading activity.

China's market closure limited export volumes to key Southeast Asian regions, while other Northeast Asian producers have yet to announce offers for November cargoes. According to some market sources, China's logistics situation has shown signs of improvement as port congestion eased and the typhoon peak season has passed, helping to reduce pressure on the supply chain in the short term. Meanwhile, operating rates at PE plants in Southeast Asia are estimated at 70%-75%.

In Vietnam, high import offers from Saudi Arabia's Sabic met strong buyer resistance. The LDPE price uptrend also showed signs of stalling as buyers grew increasingly reluctant to accept high offers. However, offer prices remain supported by prolonged supply scarcity and high freight costs.

Today, October 8, the distributor of Saudi Arabia's Qamar offered PE imports ex-bonded warehouse HCMC, with LLDPE Film and HDPE Film both at USD 1,480/tonne, equal to the LLDPE Film offer ex-bonded warehouse Hai Phong earlier this week. The distributor advised that grade LLDPE FD21HS has about 306 tonnes, LLDPE CD18N about 49.5 tonnes, and HDPE F1 about 51 tonnes. Volumes are very small, so the impact on the overall market is limited.

China resumed operations today after a one-week holiday, but not many PE offers from Chinese plants to Vietnam have been recorded. Notably, LLDPE futures on the Dalian Commodity Exchange (China) jumped nearly USD 57/tonne from the September 30 settlement price — before the holiday — and China's domestic spot LLDPE price also rose USD 45-50/tonne over the same period.

Even so, one distributor was recorded offering Saudi Arabia's Sabic HDPE Film FJ00952, re-exported from a Chinese port to Vietnam at USD 1,340/tonne/CIF Hai Phong, with an LSD of November 30 and a volume of about 204 tonnes. Another distributor offered Saudi Arabia's Sabic LLDPE Film grade 218NJ and US Sabic LLDPE Film grade 218NJA, re-exported from China to Vietnam at USD 1,320/tonne/CIF, for November 2026 shipment. This distributor's offer is up USD 10/tonne from last week's quotation. These re-exported cargoes are considerably cheaper than Sabic's direct quotations to the Vietnamese market last week.

Another distributor offered China's Petrochina Guangxi LLDPE Film 2020F, priced in VND, at VND 39,400/kg including VAT at Hai Phong port, for delivery in 5 weeks — that is, arriving around mid-November 2026.

In the domestic market, PE offers from most traders also held flat from yesterday and have not yet moved up with the price trend in China. Even so, market sentiment is more positive: hesitant buyers who had been weighing earlier prices quickly closed purchases, concerned that sellers will soon raise prices if the Chinese market keeps up its momentum over the next few sessions.
In fact, since the start of the week, transaction prices for PE products in Vietnam have trended from flat to slightly lower versus late last week, although few sellers have cut prices much.

For HDPE, yesterday LSP's office adjusted its offer for CP Chem Singapore-origin HDPE blow 5502 down slightly by VND 400/kg from last week, to VND 43,400/kg including VAT. Even so, this offer is still considered too high and few buyers are contracting imports. The reason is that a deal has been recorded for US-origin HDPE blow at only VND 39,000/kg including VAT. The lowest spot price recorded for HDPE Film is VND 39,000/kg including VAT, for Chinese material, flat since late last week. Thailand's PTT HDPE yarn 5000S was offered at around VND 41,000/kg including VAT…

For LLDPE, in fact some import cargoes of Middle Eastern LLDPE Film have arrived in scattered lots since last week, but volumes are small, enough only to deliver to customers who contracted earlier, or sellers are rushing to sell quickly to lock in profits. Spot offer volumes on the market are small, so most sellers hold offers flat from late last week, with Middle Eastern-origin LLDPE Film commonly in the VND 42,000-43,000/kg including VAT range; US-origin LLDPE Film is also offered at a high level of around VND 41,000-41,500/kg including VAT.

For LDPE, a northern seller disclosed having closed sales of Lotte Titan Malaysia LDPE Film 260GG at VND 46,000/kg including VAT to retail buyers, although the offer was up to VND 47,000/kg including VAT. Many other sellers also said LDPE Film transaction prices this week are cooling, with LDPE Film of Sabic, Tasnee, Lotte Titan, PTT… origin mainly recorded in the VND 45,000-45,500/kg including VAT range, although some sellers still offer up to VND 48,000/kg including VAT…

summary: Domestic distributor offers down; Philrex PR1000 to VND 23,500-23,600; AGC/TPC cut 300-500/kg
US Shintech SE950/SE1000 wide spread VND 23,400-24,200 (north as low as 23,200, a deep cut)
Shintech raised bid to USD 790-800 CIF, but cheap prior US cargoes (620-650) still arriving
paras: A survey today, October 8, found PVC offer prices from domestic trading distributors mostly adjusted down slightly.
In the south, one distributor offered Philrex (Philippines) PVC PR1000 down to VND 23,500-23,600/kg including VAT and delivery, after holding above VND 24,000/kg including VAT for several weeks.

Offers from the two domestic plants, AGC Vina and TPC Vina, were also adjusted down VND 300-500/kg from late September, with AGC Vina's PVC PM66R down to VND 23,800/kg including VAT and TPC Vina's PVC SG660 down to VND 24,000/kg including VAT.

Offers for US Shintech PVC SE950/SE1000 showed quite wide spreads between distributors, ranging VND 23,400-24,200/kg including VAT depending on the seller, down considerably from the start of the week.

Notably, in the north, some sellers were recorded offering US Shintech PVC SE950/SE1000 at only VND 23,200/kg including VAT and delivery, a deep cut of more than VND 1,000/kg from late September. Meanwhile, coal-based PVC held transaction prices at around VND 22,500-23,000/kg including VAT…

As reported earlier, early this week the distributor for US Shintech raised its bid-taking price for PVC SE950/SE1000 delivered to Vietnam to USD 790-800/tonne/CIF, up about USD 20/tonne from early last month. The cargo is expected to arrive in Vietnam in January 2027. The higher price is supported by Shintech's plan to temporarily halt some PVC plants for maintenance in October-November 2026.

Even so, according to sources, a significant volume of US-origin PVC SE950/SE1000 previously contracted for import at around USD 620-650/tonne is expected to arrive in the country in October. This low-priced material may add competitive pressure in the domestic market, while consumption demand has yet to genuinely improve. Therefore, even with plants about to go into maintenance, domestic PVC price levels will find it hard to rise in October.
